questions.q: Android, the mobile operating system, is built on which kernel?
questions.solution: Android uses the Linux kernel at its core with Java/Kotlin application layers on top - a standard exam fact.

questions.q: Which shortcut key runs the spelling and grammar check in MS Word?
questions.solution: F7 opens Spelling & Grammar. F5 opens Find & Replace's Go To (and starts a PowerPoint show), F9 refreshes fields, F12 is Save As.
questions.shortcut: F7 = spell-check in every Office app.

questions.q: Which tool **lists all installed hardware along with its drivers** and flags devices that are not working?
questions.solution: **Device Manager** enumerates every hardware component with its driver status — problem devices show a warning mark.

questions.q: In the extension .docx, the letter X stands for —
questions.solution: The X marks the **Office Open XML** format introduced with Office 2007 — the same X appears in .xlsx and .pptx.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said to me, "Please lend me your pen."
options: He requested me to lend him my pen.
He requested me to lend me your pen.
He ordered me to lend him my pen.
He said to me please to lend him my pen.
questions.solution: Please → **requested**; to lend + him (speaker) + my (listener). B leaves both pronouns direct; C mismatches tone (ordered for a request); D has no sentence structure.
questions.shortcut: please sets the verb: requested; then him + my.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: No sooner had the train left
questions.solution: The frozen pair is **no sooner…than**: 'No sooner had the train left **than** the passengers began…'. 'When' belongs with hardly/scarcely.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Keep the **e** before -able: noticeable. The e protects the soft 'c' sound (notice → notice-able). Noticable is the planted drop.
questions.shortcut: Keep-e rule: soft c needs its e.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The chairman, along with the directors, **were** inspecting the plant when the auditors arrived.
questions.solution: 'Along with' only adds information; the subject stays **the chairman** → **was inspecting**. The narration is past, so the present helpers in options 3 and 4 are out at once.

questions.q: The **Ryder Cup** is a team competition in which sport, contested between the USA and Europe?
questions.solution: The **Ryder Cup** is golf's USA v Europe biennial match; the Davis Cup is tennis's equivalent for nations.

questions.q: The **Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna)** of Rigvedic tradition was fought on the river —
questions.solution: The Dasarajna (Mandala VII) was fought on the **Parushni = Ravi**. **Sudas** of the Bharata clan defeated a confederacy of ten kings.

questions.q:
Match:
1. Rakhi bandhan as protest — Rabindranath Tagore
2. *Amar Sonar Bangla* — composed during Swadeshi agitation
3. National Council of Education — 1906
Which are correct?
questions.solution: All three are Swadeshi-era facts: Tagore's Rakhi tying and later the song (now Bangladesh's anthem), and the **National Council of Education (1906)** for national education.

questions.q: Which of the following substances undergoes sublimation?
questions.solution: **Camphor** changes directly from solid to vapour — **sublimation**. Naphthalene, iodine, ammonium chloride and dry ice also sublime.

questions.q: If the area of a square increases by 96%, then each of its sides increases by:
questions.solution: Side factor $=\sqrt{1.96}=1.4$, so the side increases by 40%.

questions.q: If $x-\frac1x=3$, then the value of $x^2+\frac1{x^2}$ is:
Find the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 20% per annum for 1½ years, interest compounded half-yearly.
questions.solution: Rate per half-year $= 10\%$, 3 periods → $10000 \times 1.1^3 = 13310$. CI $= ₹3{,}310$.
questions.shortcut: ₹3,000 treats it as one year at 20% plus simple half-year.

questions.q: A can do $\frac{2}{5}$ of a work in 6 days and B can do $\frac{3}{4}$ of the same work in 9 days. Working together, they complete the work in:
questions.solution:
A: full work in $\frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15$ days; B: $\frac{9 \times 4}{3} = 12$ days.
Together: $\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{20}$ ⇒ $6\frac{2}{3}$ days.
questions.shortcut: Scale each to full-work time first (15 and 12), then combine.

questions.q:
Select the term that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**D5, G10, ?, M20, P25**
questions.solution: Letters D, G, _, M, P (+3) → J. Numbers 5, 10, _, 20, 25 (+5) → 15. Answer **J15**.
questions.shortcut: Both tracks pass through the gap evenly.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**12   23   53**

**31   14   54**

**21   32   ?**
questions.solution: Reverse each input, then add: 21 + 32 = 53 ✓; 13 + 41 = 54 ✓. So 12 + 23 = **35**. (53 adds the unreversed inputs — which is exactly row 1's output, a planted trap.)
questions.shortcut: Outputs look like sums of flipped numbers → reverse first.

questions.q: In a survey, **70% of people watch cricket, 60% watch football and 40% watch both.** What percentage watch **neither**?
questions.shortcut: Percentages behave exactly like counts — total is 100.

questions.q: The figure shows the **mirror image** of a wall clock (the dot marks 12). What is the actual time?
questions.solution: The dot marks 12. Read the picture as it is: the hands show **10:15**. That is the mirror image, so the actual time = 11:60 − 10:15 = **1:45**. Check: 10:15 + 1:45 = 12:00.
questions.shortcut: Read the picture, then subtract from 11:60.
